claims.claim_en: German households face one of Europe’s highest electricity prices.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined

evidence.locator: European comparison using Eurostat second-half 2025 prices

claims.explanation: Contemporary available European comparisons place Germany near the top for the specified household consumption band. This supports one of the highest, without claiming the highest in every metric.
claims.limits: Latest comparable cross-country observations are for 2025; nominal euros differ from purchasing-power and usage-band comparisons.

claims.claim_en: The August 2026 household price for 3,500 kWh is about 37 ct/kWh versus about 33 in 2021.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined

evidence.locator: Physical pages 4,6,9: method, 37.0 in 2026 and 32.8 in 2021; chart visually inspected

claims.explanation: The recovered August analysis reproduces the rounded figures. It models available new tariffs and includes base prices; it is not an expenditure-weighted mean of all existing households. The retrieved publication date is 21 August, after the 13 August response, so the exact earlier snapshot was not authenticated.
claims.limits: Later corroboration of the values does not independently establish what was available on 13 August. No falsehood inferred.

claims.claim_en: Network charges constitute roughly one quarter of the household electricity price.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The cited model’s component share is exactly 25% at the stated rounding.
claims.limits: BDEW tariff model, not all individual contracts; later August publication confirms the component relation but not a frozen 13 August snapshot.

claims.claim_en: Additional network-related costs are recovered through separate electricity levies.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: Offshore and special-network-use levies recover costs outside the regular network-charge component.
claims.limits: The KWKG levy has a support-policy purpose and is not entirely a physical grid cost; no amount is inferred for all levies combined.

claims.claim_en: The coalition contract promises at least five cents/kWh relief and EU minimum electricity tax for all, plus lower levies/network costs.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined

evidence.locator: Physical page 32 lines956–958 and page49 lines1501–1503

claims.explanation: The official party-published agreement states these commitments.
claims.limits: Political commitment, not an enacted universal price guarantee or proof of fulfilment.

claims.claim_en: The permanent 2026 electricity-tax reduction covers manufacturing and agriculture/forestry, leaving ordinary households outside it.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The general rate is €20.50/MWh and §9b grants qualifying businesses €20/MWh relief. The special business relief does not cover ordinary household consumption.
claims.limits: Subject to application, business-use rules and the €250 retained threshold; not a statement that no household can ever qualify for a different electricity-tax exemption.

claims.claim_en: The 2026 €6.5 billion transmission subsidy contributed to lower downstream network tariffs.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The statutory subsidy lowers transmission cost recovery and the independent operator sheet shows a lower downstream household tariff than without it.
claims.limits: This establishes a tariff mechanism and example, not full immediate retail pass-through for every household.

claims.claim_en: The draft provides €5.525 billion annually in 2027–2029, almost €1 billion less than 2026.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The proposed amount and duration match; €6.5−€5.525 =€0.975 billion per year.
claims.limits: Current public draft bears internal 3 August 2026 12:48 timestamp; byte identity with initial consultation dispatch is not independently authenticated. Assessed at the authored August date.

claims.claim_en: The proposal requires network operators to publish tariffs with and without subsidy and suppliers to flag the subsidy in annual invoices.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The operative wording contains the transmission and distribution comparison and the supplier invoice notice.
claims.limits: The duty is information; it is not by itself a new rule of immediate retail price reduction.

claims.claim_en: The April market check found mean annual household savings of €56 in the examined networks.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined

evidence.locator: Independent 2026 operator sheet confirms method of hypothetical tariff comparison

claims.explanation: The source surveys 25 operators, with a 3,500 kWh model household and unweighted network comparisons. Its stated mean is €56 before VAT; the author explicitly limits this to examined networks.
claims.limits: No complete underlying 25-operator data table was published here for independent replication of the mean. Sample selection by circuit length and city density is not a nationally representative household weighting.

claims.claim_en: The government sought roughly €100 household electricity savings per year through the subsidy.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined

evidence.locator: Government page, 3 September2026 update: model3,500kWh can yield about€100

claims.explanation: The current official page confirms a conditional calculation around €100 and the April source cites an earlier government announcement. The precise 2025 version was not recovered, and can amount to €100 is weaker than a universal target.
claims.limits: Later official page is corroboration, not an authenticated earlier copy. Preserve the difference between a potential model saving and a guaranteed outcome.

claims.claim_en: Household savings differ substantially by region and are lower than industry savings in the comparison.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined

evidence.locator: Physical pages5,7: household7–26%,18–109euros; industry average25% versus household15%
Sections2,4: cascade and different tariff levels

claims.explanation: The author study reports percentage reductions in 25 networks, while tariff rules and independent operator data confirm unequal effects by level and region.
claims.limits: The industrial comparison is a 24 GWh/6,000 hour model; relative percentage benefit is different from euros per customer or per kWh. Not every industrial firm is covered equally.

claims.claim_en: The subsidy cut is caused by reallocations in KTF toward industrial relief.

claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined

evidence.locator: Official parliamentary report17August2026: network, compensation and industry-price titles

claims.explanation: The draft allocations move in the described directions, but matching amounts do not by themselves establish that one title directly financed another. An explicit primary budget decision attributing that causal reallocation was not obtained.
claims.limits: The report was published after the response; it corroborates plan amounts rather than proving the earlier causal attribution.

claims.claim_en: KTF 2027 plans about €5 billion electricity-price compensation, roughly €1 billion more, plus about €2.4 billion industrial-price spending.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The official parliamentary report reproduces the government draft with the stated rounded values.
claims.limits: Report published17 August after the response; checks budget-plan content, not contemporaneous publication or final enacted expenditure. Industrial-price direct eligibility differs from indirect household effects.

claims.claim_en: Verivox calculates a roughly 0.25 ct/kWh net increase from cutting the network subsidy by about €1 billion.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The original analyst describes a proportional scenario: about 1.7 ct from 6.5 billion implies about 0.26 ct per billion, consistent with rounded 0.25. Vzbv accurately identifies it as a Verivox calculation.
claims.limits: Scenario assumes comparable tariffs and pass-through. It is not an observed 2027 price change; all 850 operator raw inputs were not supplied for independent reconstruction.

claims.claim_en: The named electricity levies are charged to ordinary private households at the same nationwide per-kWh rates.

evidence.locator: Section3.4 and 4.3, uniform levies and privileged-user exceptions

claims.explanation: The three levies use nationwide rates for non-privileged household consumption. Equal height is read as the unit rate, consistent with the paragraph.
claims.limits: Absolute euro payments vary with consumption; special statutory privileges and exemptions are separate.

claims.claim_en: The Commission proposes lower taxation of electricity than natural gas.

evidence.locator: COM(2026)600 explanatory memorandum and proposed tax principles

claims.explanation: The primary proposal and Commission summary state the favourable electricity-versus-gas tax objective.

claims.claim_en: Reducing household electricity tax to the EU minimum and removing the named levies yields about €171 annual saving for the model household.
claims.policy_link: Household relief, uniform levies and enforceable pass-through
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined

evidence.locator: Annex I Table C: non-business electricity €1/MWh =0.1 ct/kWh

claims.explanation: The arithmetic is (2.05−0.1+0.446+0.941+1.559)ct×3,500 kWh=€171.36 before VAT. This reproduces the calculation from independently checked components.
claims.limits: Before VAT and with complete pass-through; including 19% VAT would give about €203.92. The text cites a calculation rather than an actual universal bill reduction.

claims.claim_en: The 2022EEG-levy law required dated price reductions in basic and other supply contracts under EnWG §118(37)–(38).

claims.explanation: The law required basic-supply price reductions and qualifying outside-basic-supply reductions on 1 July 2022; the neighbouring paragraph 39 extends rules to other qualifying cases.

claims.claim_en: The proposal’s information duties do not themselves ensure immediate full household pass-through.

evidence.locator: §118(5) lower net cost balance at next contractual adjustment

claims.explanation: The draft adds transparency rather than a dated automatic price-reduction duty. Existing law requires a lower cost balance to enter the next contractual adjustment, which is distinct from immediate full pass-through.
claims.limits: Do not infer absence of all pre-existing pass-through obligations. Whether stronger enforcement should be adopted is the author’s preference.

claims.claim_en: Draft §24d provides €5.525 billion/year for 2027–2029,€16.575 billion total, funded by KTF.

claims.explanation: This is an accurate attribution of the draft’s reasoning.

claims.explanation: The entitlement, proportional allocation, instalments and cost-recovery approach continue the existing model.

claims.claim_en: The subsidy effectively relieves all electricity-consuming grid users, including downstream customers.

claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined

evidence.locator: §14 vertical cost allocation and§19 special tariffs
Sections4.1–4.3: some regional savings vanish or are very small

claims.explanation: The cost cascade extends across voltage levels in principle, but magnitude can approach zero in some regions and retail pass-through depends on contracts and cost balances. Universal effective relief for every user is not established.
claims.limits: Read charitably as general reach of the tariff mechanism. No error admitted from a conversational universal when indirect levy effects and user circumstances remain unquantified.

claims.claim_en: Relief differs regionally because network conditions and tariff cascades differ.

claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined

claims.claim_en: Network transformation entails large transmission and distribution investments.

evidence.locator: Rationale on rising network costs and financing

claims.explanation: Regulatory monitoring documents substantial ongoing investment and expansion requirements at both levels.

claims.claim_en: TSOs publish preliminary following-year tariffs around1 October, while downstream tariffs must be published by15 October.

claims.explanation: The statute establishes the15 October deadline; the draft separately identifies1 OctoberTSOpublication practice used by downstream operators.

claims.claim_en: The draft provides a safeguard if subsidy payment fails or becomes legally impossible.

claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The provision permits a once-yearly adjustment in the specified nonpayment/legal cases.
claims.limits: Calling it ultima ratio or seeking stronger funding certainty is normative; the law is not a blanket discretion to cancel funding.

claims.claim_en: Proposed §118(5b) requires distribution operators’ hypothetical no-subsidy tariffs and suppliers’ invoice notices.
claims.policy_link: Stable network-cost subsidy and practical implementation
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: Both specific information duties are present.
claims.limits: No quantified new bureaucratic burden is asserted as verified.

claims.claim_en: The draft continues the subsidy to 2029 and adds no direct EEG amendment or new project-developer duty.

claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The bill amends EnWG subsidy/information rules and commencement. It neither amends EEG nor assigns new duties specifically to renewable developers.
claims.limits: Indirect effects on developers through tariffs or investment incentives remain possible.

claims.claim_en: The latest Monopolkommission report favours broad electricity-price relief over narrow beneficiary support.
claims.policy_link: Broad electricity-price relief and structural efficiency
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The primary report favours horizontal, cross-sector relief over fragmented special rules, while retaining limited exceptions.
claims.limits: A policy recommendation in a study, not proof every broad subsidy is optimal or every targeted measure inferior.

claims.claim_en: Electricity prices remain high in international comparison in 2026.
claims.policy_link: Broad electricity-price relief and structural efficiency
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: Available primary material supports a historically high German position and current German prices, but the directly comparable international observations are principally 2025. The exact 2026 international ranking/cohort is unspecified.
claims.limits: No error inferred from mixed data years; household, industry, wholesale and purchasing-power comparisons differ.

claims.claim_en: The subsidy shifts tariff funding to public money without itself reforming the tariff system or funding a specific new grid/storage project.
claims.policy_link: Broad electricity-price relief and structural efficiency
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The operative mechanism pays part of existing tariff cost recovery. Structural tariff redesign proceeds separately.
claims.limits: This is a direct mechanism claim, not a conclusion that subsidies have no indirect investment or behavioural effects.

claims.claim_en: The Commission has proposed changes to electricity-market regulation that impose conditions on state network-cost funding.
claims.policy_link: Compatibility with new EU and national tariff regulation
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The official proposal permits partial state funding subject to nondiscrimination, preserved incentives, temporary additional-cost scope and competition conditions.
claims.limits: The authors cautiously say compatibility may be interpreted as problematic. They do not claim an outright ban; actual compatibility is a legal question left open.

claims.claim_en: AgNes draft published6 August proposes new payer categories from 1 January 2029 including generation, storage and electrolysers.
claims.policy_link: Compatibility with new EU and national tariff regulation
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The draft begins in 2029 and introduces category-specific financing/capacity tariffs.
claims.limits: Generator size thresholds, grandfathering, storage configuration and existing exemptions matter; not every existing asset pays immediately.

claims.claim_en: The ministry rationale says annual subsidy reconciliation uses regulatory-account approval and balances over/under-recovery there.
claims.policy_link: Compatibility with new EU and national tariff regulation
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The original rationale expressly identifies regulatory accounts and retains the fixed annual subsidy amount.
claims.limits: Description of the draft rationale, not approval of its consistency with future regulation.

claims.claim_en: The proposed TSO framework no longer considers continuation of a regulatory account necessary from 2029.
claims.policy_link: Compatibility with new EU and national tariff regulation
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: Paragraph 133 expressly states that annual plan-versus-actual reporting and interest tracking make the separate regulatory account unnecessary.
claims.limits: Draft rather than final framework; transitional balances from earlier periods are treated separately in paragraphs134–135.

claims.claim_en: The proposal continues subsidy at €5.525 billion/year for 2027–2029 compared with €6.5 billion in 2026.

claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The amounts, duration and reduction match the operative provisions.
claims.limits: Current public draft bears internal 3 August 2026 12:48 timestamp; byte identity with initial consultation dispatch is not independently authenticated. Assessed at the authored August date.

claims.claim_en: Holding other cost components comparable, the €0.975 billion cut leaves roughly €1 billion more to be funded through tariffs.
claims.policy_link: Electricity incentives, fair distribution and system flexibility
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: This follows directly from cost-recovery arithmetic. The author explicitly states the other-things-equal condition.
claims.limits: No prediction that actual aggregate 2027 tariffs must rise by exactly that amount regardless of demand, recognised costs or other measures.

claims.claim_en: Fossil fuel consumption is currently receiving price relief.
claims.policy_link: Electricity incentives, fair distribution and system flexibility
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The pre-author-date EnWG provision removes the gas-storage levy and requires qualifying price reductions. This supplies a concrete contemporary example.
claims.limits: Not a quantified claim about the net direction of every fossil tax or support instrument.

claims.claim_en: The power-plant strategy provides financial support for gas-based capacity.
claims.policy_link: Electricity incentives, fair distribution and system flexibility
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The enacted capacity framework includes gas-fired long-duration capacity and remuneration, with decarbonisation requirements.
claims.limits: Technology and hydrogen-readiness obligations are relevant; a capacity payment is not an unconditional subsidy per unit of fossil fuel burned.

claims.claim_en: Transmission subsidies disproportionately benefit large users, while levy subsidies tend to benefit smaller users more.
claims.policy_link: Electricity incentives, fair distribution and system flexibility
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The study identifies higher average proportional relief for directly connected large users and uniform levy relief for nonprivileged users; tariff rules independently support the mechanism.
claims.limits: Conditional on current system and chosen denominator; individual§19 tariffs can dampen industrial benefits. Not a universal ranking of each firm against each household.

claims.claim_en: Flexibility can improve grid use and reduce redispatch/curtailment costs in addition to grid expansion.
claims.policy_link: Electricity incentives, fair distribution and system flexibility
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: Locationally and temporally appropriate changes to demand/storage can reduce constrained flows and costly intervention. Both primary regulatory design and independent commission analysis identify the mechanism.
claims.limits: Potential rather than guaranteed savings; market-oriented flexibility can also worsen local congestion if badly located or timed.

claims.claim_en: The draft grants €5.525 billion annually for three years, nearly €1 billion below 2026.
claims.policy_link: Broad and regionally balanced electricity-cost relief
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The amount, duration and difference are correct.
claims.limits: Current public draft bears internal 3 August 2026 12:48 timestamp; byte identity with initial consultation dispatch is not independently authenticated. Assessed at the authored August date.

claims.claim_en: Electricity remains expensive internationally and relative to fossil energy.
claims.policy_link: Broad and regionally balanced electricity-cost relief
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: International evidence depends on year, user band, tax and purchasing power. Relative fossil comparisons also require efficiencies and useful-energy output, which the statement does not define.

claims.claim_en: Network charges account for up to25%of prices for household, business and smaller industrial users.

claims.claim_en: Subsidy effects differ substantially with network level and region.

claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The regulator’s published draft explicitly sets 2029 implementation.
claims.limits: Proposal, not final; preparation recommendation is normative.

claims.claim_en: The proposal reduces annual subsidy from €6.5 billion in 2026to €5.525 billionfrom 2027.

claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The proposed cut matches the law and draft.
claims.limits: Authored18 August; do not infer individual submission/delivery timing from the ministry’s reported consultation window.

claims.claim_en: A politically formulated industrial-electricity goal is €50/MWh inclusive of network charges and all state price components.
claims.policy_link: Industrial electricity-cost relief and individual tariffs
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The official instrument targets a wholesale-price reference and compensation for eligible consumption, not an all-inclusive retail guarantee. However, the author does not name the speaker or specific political statement and repeatedly advocates an all-inclusive objective.
claims.limits: Do not turn a policy demand or unspecified political attribution into an error about the government scheme without authenticating the intended promise.

claims.claim_en: Individual network tariffs can reduce or eliminate the subsidy benefit for some industrial users.
claims.policy_link: Industrial electricity-cost relief and individual tariffs
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The regulatory system permits company-specific tariff treatment and therefore differing relief. The precise zero-benefit case depends on physical-path costs, minimum floors and contracts, which were not reconstructed for a specific facility.
claims.limits: The modal can statement is plausible; no claim of actual zero effect at thyssenkrupp is verified or contradicted.

claims.claim_en: The draft permits a within-year tariff adjustment if subsidy payment fails.
claims.policy_link: Industrial electricity-cost relief and individual tariffs
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The provision permits a joint TSO decision to adjust once within a year in defined nonpayment/legal cases, with notices.
claims.limits: The broader language about revocation is a policy concern; the draft does not grant unrestricted discretion to revoke payment.

claims.claim_en: The consultation period available to the counties was only about one week.
claims.policy_link: Municipal relief, system-cost reduction and regional coordination
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The reported general interval is approximately one week, but the actual individual invitation/receipt and deadline were not authenticated.
claims.limits: No inference of exact individual recipient time or timely delivery from public list inclusion; briefness/adequacy is a policy assessment.

claims.claim_en: The draft pays €5.525 billion/year for three years from KTF.
claims.policy_link: Municipal relief, system-cost reduction and regional coordination
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: Amount, term and funding purpose match the public draft.
claims.limits: Current public draft bears internal 3 August 2026 12:48 timestamp; byte identity with initial consultation dispatch is not independently authenticated. Assessed at the authored August date.

claims.claim_en: The subsidy changes who finances network costs rather than directly reducing system costs.
claims.policy_link: Municipal relief, system-cost reduction and regional coordination
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The direct accounting mechanism pays part of recognised costs from KTF and reduces costs recovered through network tariffs. It does not itself remove the underlying physical costs.
claims.limits: Not a conclusion that no indirect behavioural, cost-of-capital or investment effect could ever occur.

claims.claim_en: The subsidy falls by €975 million or15%compared with 2026.
claims.policy_link: Municipal relief, system-cost reduction and regional coordination
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: €6.5 billion−€5.525 billion=€0.975 billion, and0.975/6.5=15%.
claims.limits: Current public draft bears internal 3 August 2026 12:48 timestamp; byte identity with initial consultation dispatch is not independently authenticated. Assessed at the authored August date.

claims.claim_en: Transmission costs include expansion/capital costs and congestion-management/redispatch components.
claims.policy_link: Municipal relief, system-cost reduction and regional coordination
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: Primary regulation and monitoring identify those cost components and their connection to flows, capacity and coordination.
claims.limits: No percentage allocation or proof every additional cost is avoidable is asserted.

claims.claim_en: Coordinating local generation, demand, storage and sector coupling can reduce upstream grid use and expansion needs.
claims.policy_link: Municipal relief, system-cost reduction and regional coordination
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: Appropriately timed and located demand/generation matching can reduce simultaneous upstream peaks and binding capacity requirements. The statement explicitly makes the claim conditional.
claims.limits: Annual local energy balance alone is not enough; the time and location profile and network topology determine benefits.

claims.claim_en: Regulated network operation allows recognised returns on equity and regulated revenue recovery.
claims.policy_link: Municipal relief, system-cost reduction and regional coordination
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The regulatory framework recognises a calculated equity return and cost-recovery mechanisms.
claims.limits: Allowed returns are conditional on recognition and regulation; not a guaranteed profit for any asset or operator.

claims.claim_en: Regional municipal energy projects face substantial development, financing and marketing risks relative to regulated networks.
claims.policy_link: Municipal relief, system-cost reduction and regional coordination
claims.check_method: Full original re-read before earlier dispositions; independent primary-law/data checks; source methods, date, cohort and conditional mechanisms examined
claims.explanation: The regulatory difference supports a plausible distinction, but sources do not quantify actual municipal project risks or establish the broad comparative magnitude.
claims.limits: No representative municipal project financing or outcome dataset was obtained; policy judgment about an unfair imbalance is excluded.

exclusions.reason: Policy demands for equal household relief, tax/levy cuts and immediate enforcement are preferences. Assessments of inadequate or unfair relief are judgments; the numerical and legal premises are inventoried. Impressum, contacts and registration information are incidental.
The 2027 retail-price increase is a forecast. The attributed Verivox calculation and its assumptions are checked as a model description, not an observed future outcome.
Title, contents, authored date, member-market shares, registration and compliance boilerplate are low-priority organisational description.

Welcome, planning certainty, expected future jobs and benefits of modernisation are policy framing or forecasts. Faster legislation, predicted customer uncertainty and requests to remove information duties are preferences or predictions. Specific legal, timing and funding premises are inventoried.

The desirability of electrification, defossilisation, sovereignty and structural reform are policy judgments. Future prices not falling and predicted renewable-expansion effects are forecasts. Contacts are incidental.

Compatibility with future EU law is expressly a cautious interpretation and request for amendment, not a categorical ban claim. Requests for 2029 clarification and an annual reconciliation option are proposals. Actual draft premises are inventoried.

Calls for faster electrification, energy independence, a €6.5 billion subsidy and removal of fossil subsidies are preferences. Future investment responses and required political ambition are predictions or judgments. Conditional cost and flexibility mechanisms were checked separately.
Desired tax and levy reductions, the judgment that the cut is inappropriate and future planning benefits are preferences or forecasts. Contact and registration details are incidental.

The possibility that the cut fully offsets industrial-price relief is explicitly conditional and prospective. Without a firm-level model it cannot be a factual error. Requests for an all-inclusive €50 goal, stable funding and public financing of transformation costs are preferences. The 18 August authored date is preserved without a delivery inference.

Adequacy of consultation, need for an overall plan, insufficient recognition of regional actors and requests for pilots, energy sharing or fair conditions are policy judgments. Forecasts of acceptance, resilience, value creation and profitability are excluded. Concrete financing and physical mechanisms are inventoried. Footer population and budget boilerplate is low priority.

limitations: No human specialist review or author contact.
Current ministry draft has an internal 3 August timestamp; initial dispatch bytes are not independently authenticated.
Thyssenkrupp is authored 18 August, outside the reported 5–13 August consultation window; actual delivery timing is not inferred.
The recovered BDEW August PDF was published 21 August, after most responses. The values corroborate the statements but earlier snapshot identity remains unverified.
Vzbv’s 25-network mean is not a population-weighted national mean. Its savings are before VAT. A source calculation differs from realised retail pass-through.
Radware challenge pages, empty 202 responses and non-PDF contents are marked unusable. Tool extraction archives are explicit.
Private contracts, individual industrial tariff cases, comparative project risks and causal budget reallocation remain unverified.
